study_type: preregistered policy comparison on an operator-approved collection
experimental_unit: one approved PDF classified by pdf-inspector, with routing replayed under four policies

baseline_exp28.description: historical policy exactly as experiment 28 evaluated it: pre-fix unconditional set plus its 0.5/0.5 thresholds, pinned at the pre-fix revision

baseline_matched.description: pre-fix unconditional set at the approved 0.5/0.10 thresholds; differs from candidate only in the unconditional set, isolating the 9bf4810 fix

candidate.description: committed post-fix policy (9bf4810) at the operator-approved 0.5/0.10 thresholds

enable_only.description: committed unconditional set with both thresholds at the 0.0 never-trigger sentinels — the behaviour when only OCR_FALLBACK_ENABLED is set

collection.source: explicit operator-approved path list only; no directory scan
collection.membership: 3 development (the exp-28 book + the two known needs-OCR papers) + 14 held-out (the operator's Zotero 'RAG' collection PDFs)
collection.held_out_disclosure: all 14 held-out documents were inside experiment 28's corpus: their classification evidence predates this freeze, but none routed and none were individually examined during candidate design; their independent labels are new evidence. They test the safety gate only — no held-out document needs OCR, so held-out recall is reported as untested.

labels.method: independent page assessment via a second extractor (pypdf, distinct from pdf-inspector): per-page text density plus image-only detection; every page pdf-inspector flagged is checked, plus a sample of unflagged pages; uncertain cases recorded explicitly
labels.split_rule: development documents may guide the candidate; held-out outcomes are withheld from candidate design

routing_judgements.missing_page_tolerance: 10% of pages lacking usable text warrants whole-document OCR (candidate page_fraction = 0.10)
routing_judgements.whole_document_routing: whole-file dispatch accepted — no page stitching exists; a document above tolerance is OCR'd in full
routing_judgements.enable_only_zero_threshold: a mixed PDF with thresholds at the 0.0 sentinels stays on the fast path — classification-only routing, matching the committed code

ocr_authorisation.note: classification and routing replay only; OCR cost is reported as a projection and recovery quality as unmeasured

ground_truth_definition.label: needs_ocr
ground_truth_definition.rule: independent page assessment in labels.json — never the classifier output and never aggregate character counts alone; a document is needs_ocr=true when the share of pages without usable text meets the 10% tolerance

cells.role: regression checks; may guide the candidate
independent validation; outcomes withheld during design

gate_freeze.foreknowledge_of_data: The experiment-28 documents are known: the book (991 pages, mixed, false-routed), the scanned Kerr 1998 paper and the zero-extract Sloman 1971 paper. All three are development evidence only. The 14 held-out documents' classification evidence predates this freeze but their outcomes did not guide the candidate and their labels are new.

baseline_evidence.experiment_28: experiments/28-pdf-classification-prevalence-2026-09-09/results.md — FAIL on both gates under the pre-fix policy
baseline_evidence.ocr_cost: ocr-worker/SMOKE_RESULTS.md — 33.7 to 106.4 s per page warm

validity_gates.definition: held-out documents with needs_ocr == false that the candidate policy routes to OCR
validity_gates.basis: same zero-tolerance principle as experiments 24 and 28: a false route costs 33.7-106.4 s per page against a ~1 s fast path

validity_gates.definition: held-out documents with needs_ocr == true that the candidate policy leaves on the fast path
validity_gates.basis: a promoted default that misses genuinely textless documents preserves the gap it exists to close
validity_gates.known_limitation: no held-out document is expected to carry needs_ocr=true, so this gate is expected to be untestable on held-out evidence; the development split carries the recall check (Kerr and Sloman must route)

monitored_non_gating.definition: routed pages x 106.4 s, labelled a projection — no real OCR is authorised
monitored_non_gating.reason: cost evidence for the promotion decision; never gated
actual cost of the measurement itself

monitored_non_gating.definition: documents where routed_baseline_matched differs from routed_candidate
monitored_non_gating.reason: isolates what the 9bf4810 fix changes on real documents at the approved thresholds

decision_rule.supports_promotion: safety gate passes on held-out evidence AND both dev recall checks (Kerr, Sloman) route under the candidate
decision_rule.promote_nothing: the safety gate fails, or a dev recall check misses
decision_rule.note: promotion is a separate later decision informed by this study; this change never promotes a packaged default
